NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1273 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.
  • Sources indicate that most headlines on NEAR’s fresh inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number.
  • House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Industry observers note that HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Sources indicate that most headlines on NEAR’s fresh inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:.

cap(t) = 2.5% − 0.9% × min(t, 24) / 24.

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:.

The yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

Recent findings suggest that latest tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:.

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio.

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

Recent findings suggest that the formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Industry observers note that stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every latest token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Industry observers note that validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to initiative. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics noted the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

According to recent reports, two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a new proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

In a recent development, ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to enhancement their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Industry observers note that price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anthropic’s post-IPO performance appears to have created a volatile market setup.

Sources indicate that on the technical side, ANT opened at $111.50, around 34% above its $83 IPO price, before losing much of its early gains and closing at $97.17. This shows that initial demand was strong, but profit-taking promptly kicked in. The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

Sources indicate that naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility? Interestingly, recent Glassnode data points to a possible link. As the chart below reveals, Anthropic futures on crypto platforms recorded $9.5 billion in trading volume ahead of its Nasdaq debut. In comparison, SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, attracted $3.9 billion in pre-listing futures volume before its June debut.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

This highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a upcoming record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype promptly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

In a recent development, so, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

Industry observers note that according to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

Worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

It has been revealed that why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

It has been revealed that so, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

ANT’s IPO may have added to Bitcoin’s fear and increased crypto selling.

Weak liquidity could keep pressure on crypto, putting the $2 trillion market cap at risk.

In a recent development, in an X post, Fidelity Investments' Director of Global Macro, Jurrien Timmer, says he remains bullish on Bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math. Timmer isn't oblivious to Bitcoin's recent poor performance, which he highlighted in a separate X post.

According to recent reports, "I would be remiss if I didn’t mention Bitcoin and its very poor price action. It has gotten significantly more correlated to the S&P 500 in recent weeks, trading more like a speculative risk asset than a monetary asset," Timmer wrote.

Industry observers note that timmer added that Bitcoin has a dual personality in his own view, consisting of a monetary factor and a speculative factor. He depicted this by showing the rate of change in the GS non-profitable tech basket and the global money supply. When both are expanding rapidly, Bitcoin moons, and vice versa. Right now, risk appetites are receding as the AI theme corrects, while global liquidity is also receding, Timmer explained.

Industry observers note that in his post, Timmer pointed out that Bitcoin is back on the Power Law support curve, which he claims is a 'bit disheartening.' He highlighted the significance of this, saying that if Bitcoin’s price were ever to fall well below this support line, which is currently at $62,000 and rising, it would put his entire framework in doubt. "Never a dull moment!" he added.

Recent findings suggest that I remain bullish on Bitcoin based on its four-year cycle and Power Law math, but it’s a bit disheartening that we are back again sitting on that power law support curve. If Bitcoin’s price were to ever fall well below this support line (right now at $62k and rising), it would put my entire framework in doubt. Never a dull moment!

Timmer's viewpoint seems to align with that of veteran trader Peter Brandt, who noted that Bitcoin might have entered a "dicey" price range owing to its recent drop. "The territory below this level gets very dicey," he noted, underlining the $57,803 price point for Bitcoin.

It has been revealed that in September 2026, Timmer pointed to a potential double-bottom formation near $60,000, noting that breaking past resistance near $80,000–$86,000 would support a push toward $100,000. Timmer also projects Bitcoin could reach $300,000 by 2029 based on a power-law model.

Bitcoin now trades well below $62,000, and this raises the question of whether the framework underpinning Timmer’s outlook still holds.

Regardless, the long-term sentiment of crypto investors has already been sullied due to the October 29 Binance hack that resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen funds.

  • The bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways.
  • Bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s largest banking group, Intesa Sanpaolo, increased its spot altcoin ETF holdings according to a newly introduced disclosure. This follows capital rotation out of Bitcoin products by a slew of traditional firms amid dwindling market sentiment.

The bank’s disclosed crypto ETF holdings grew in Q3 2026 to $108.56 million, up $17 million, while digital asset prices moved sideways. In June, total assets were worth $90 million as it looked to diversify and grow holdings systematically.

Bitcoin, the largest asset in the portfolio, was reduced to make room for altcoins in a possible bid to diversify assets. At the end of Q2, BTC holdings stood at $69.32 million but dropped slightly to above $61 million last quarter. The firm’s Ethereum exposure also dropped to $5 million.

Industry observers note that however, Solana and XRP products filled the vacuum, highlighting institutional appetite for these assets. At the time of writing, the bank’s spot Solana ETF exposure is at $14.1 million after its investment in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF ballooned from seven shares to 875,407 shares.

Intesa’s XRP investment also grew over the same period to $27.2 million, driven mainly by 402,750 shares in the Bitwise XRP ETF. The manufacturer’s shares in the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF remained unchanged across both quarters.

More broadly, the bank reduced its Bitcoin ETF exposure and increased SOL and XRP products. Most experts believe it follows the current market trend, and firms, especially traditional companies, need to diversify to make up for Bitcoin’s decline.

According to recent reports, historically, during bear phases, there’s a huge rotation of capital into altcoins, though it’s not sustained for long. As expected, Solana and XRP become institutional favorites, while Ethereum trades similarly to Bitcoin.

Recent findings suggest that the former have the potential to record spikes within the red wave, like in 2022 before the approval of spot ETF products in the United States. These products opened up digital assets to a upcoming stash of traditional capital.

Intesa and other banks have since increased their crypto exposure, driven by the need to diversify assets and a broader adoption spree. Heightened institutional and retail interests pushed Bitcoin to an all-time high above $125k last year. Currently, BTC trades at $63,819, while Ethereum is slightly below $1,800.

The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by volume, Binance is witnessing a rapid surge in its futures trading activity as the broader crypto market continues to face increased selling pressure.

While the market is still struggling with volatility and rapidly declining investor interest, the latest on-chain data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals that futures traders have become extremely active on Binance.

The data reveals that both Bitcoin and Ethereum have seen their perpetual futures trading volume on Binance surge to a combined high of $39.8 billion as of November 20.

Notably, this marks the highest level the metric has reached since September 21, indicating that traders are actively adjusting their positions to hedge against further losses as volatility continues to intensify.

Nonetheless, Bitcoin saw the highest increase in perpetual futures volume as it surged to $24.75 billion on the same day.

The data further demonstrated that the volume was slightly higher than the $24.57 billion recorded on September 21, when Bitcoin was trading above $87,000.

Ethereum, on the other hand, followed with a notable increase in the same metric, recording $15.05 billion in perpetual futures volume on the same day.

However, Ethereum did not entirely mimic Bitcoin in the trend as this was still below the $17.27 billion recorded during the September 21 trading period.

Further data indicates that the high futures trading activity recorded on Binance on November 20 has coincided with BlackRock’s record Bitcoin ETF outflow.

The data indicates that BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $511 million in net outflows on that day, marking a sharp reversal from the positive inflows seen in September.

While this demonstrates that investors are also pulling their funds from Bitcoin ETFs, it marked the highest single-day outflow BlackRock has ever recorded.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The newly introduced Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ covered 539 miles without stopping to charge, making range anxiety look like a thing of the past.

Mercedes-Benz overhauled the EQS electric sedan, including a bigger battery and an 800V electrical architecture.

The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+ uses a 122 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 467 miles.

Sources indicate that while that’s already impressive, the electric sedan will likely go even farther in everyday driving conditions. During Edmunds recent EV Range Test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ drove a whopping 539 miles without stopping to charge.

The EQS beat its own EPA estimate by 72 miles and is now the longest-range electric sedan Edmunds has ever tested, beating the Lucid Air, the first EV to break the 500-mile mark. The only EV that has it beat is the Cadillac Escalade IQ, which managed 558 miles from its massive 205 kWh battery.

During the test, the 2027 Mercedes EQS 450+ was also more efficient than its official numbers suggest.

It has been revealed that the upcoming EQS used 29.6 kWh per 100 miles, beating its EPA estimate of 28 kWh per 100 miles. In comparison, the 2025 Mercedes EQS 450+ covered 464 miles and used 34 kWh per 100 miles during the same test, so the improvements are considerable.

Edmunds observed a peak charging rate of 350 kW, in line with Mercedes’ estimates, while it sustained an average of 222 kW throughout the session.

Both beat the older EQS, which reached a peak charge rate of 208 kW and sustained an average of 175 kW.

The upcoming Mercedes EQS 450+ added 825 miles of range in an hour, and 100 miles in just over 7 minutes, nearly twice the speed of the 2025MY.

The Edmunds EV Range Test is designed to provide a more accurate estimate of an EV’s range in everyday driving conditions. It includes 60% city and 40% highway driving with an average speed of 40 mph. The vehicle stays within 5 mph of the posted speed limit, and the climate control is set to auto at 72 degrees.

How much is too much? 539 miles on a single charge is impressive, but do you need it? In a recent “nationally representative” survey, BMW found that Americans want more EV range than they actually need.

Recent findings suggest that the study revealed that 73% consider 25, 50, or 75 miles enough to cover their daily driving. However, 42% mentioned they would require at least 300 miles of range before they would consider an EV.

In a recent development, if you have access to a home charger, nothing beats waking up with a full charge every day. Meanwhile, public charging continues to improve, giving EV drivers more reliable options on longer trips.

Industry observers note that faster charging also helps. Another 53% mentioned they would be more likely to consider an EV if it could add about 150 miles of range in around 10 minutes.

Industry observers note that in the same Edmunds EV Range Test last week, the new 2027 BMW iX3 50 xDrive drove 436 miles on a single charge, exceeding its EPA estimate of 392 miles by 44 miles. It also used 28.3 kWh per 100 miles during the test, beating its official EPA estimate of 32 kWh per 100 miles.

It has been revealed that I'm really glad to see more articles like this and people talking more about efficiency. It's not just about bigger batteries and range. It needs to be about smaller batteries plus great efficiency giving that same range. We need to do this with more efficient designs, more sedans and lighter vehicles.

The upcoming 2027 Volvo EX60 drove 352 miles while the 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric covered 392 miles during the same test.

One thing is certain: electric vehicles are becoming more efficient, enabling longer driving ranges and faster charging times. As battery tech advances, EVs will drive farther and charge faster, while safety and performance will continue to improve.

How much driving range would you consider enough for your daily drive? What about for the week? Let us know in the comments below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased.
  • According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.
  • The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period. Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Sources indicate that together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being remarked, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

Industry observers note that wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Sources indicate that institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

That mentioned, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

Industry observers note that this comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.

  • Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some customers claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin reportedly became available at a massive discount on Kraken after a sharp dislocation in Kraken's dollar trading markets.

Customers reported being able to purchase BTC for as little as 24,250 CAD, equivalent to $16,900 at that time.

Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some customers claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.

The cause the glitch is still unclear, while the reported transactions are yet to be verified.

The incident might have involved thin liquidity problem in Kraken's CAD order books.

Large sell orders reportedly overwhelmed available buy orders, leaving insufficient demand to absorb the selling pressure.

According to some accounts, at one point about 20 BTC was being sold every 15 minutes, causing the imbalance to push BTC price against CAD further down.

It has been revealed that one such transaction resulted in BTC price at around C$24,250, or $16,900. Compared with Bitcoin trading between $57,000-$58,000, the discount amounted to a staggering 71%. Other people reported BTC briefly trading around $27,000.

Kraken's status page continued to show its systems as operational during the incident. No official explanation from the exchange was available at the time of writing.

The reported dislocation highlights the risks associated with trading in markets with limited liquidity. When an order book lacks sufficient buy-side depth, even relatively large sell orders can cause prices to move sharply away from the broader market.

Recent findings suggest that on Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

Industry observers note that liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20.

According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

It has been revealed that bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions. Ethereum (ETH) fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations.

Binance accounted for 45.8% of all liquidations, and the largest single order was also on Binance: an $11.98 million ETH/USDT long position that was liquidated at $1,638.78.

It has been revealed that the crypto market today is staging a sharp recovery after Bitcoin plunged to a two-year low, triggering aggressive selling across digital assets. Bitcoin price rebounded more than 8% from its intraday low of $55,326 and briefly reclaimed $60,000, while major altcoins also recovered. However, the recovery comes against a backdrop of weakening institutional demand, heavy ETF withdrawals and a broader retreat from risk assets, leaving investors questioning whether the latest rally marks a genuine reversal or simply a temporary rebound.

Industry observers note that bitcoin price recovered sharply after falling to $55,326, its lowest level since September 2024. The cryptocurrency subsequently bounced above $60,000, recovering a significant portion of its intraday losses as buyers stepped in following the steep decline.

It has been revealed that the sell-off had pushed BTC below its previous bear-market low near $57,742, breaking a level that had held since September 2024. Bitcoin has also lost more than half its value from its record high near $126,200 reached in October 2025, highlighting the scale of the correction.

The rebound has offered short-term relief, but Bitcoin remains vulnerable after a weekly decline and a broader deterioration in market sentiment.

The recovery extended across major cryptocurrencies, although the rebound followed substantial losses earlier in the session. The broad-based recovery suggests traders are attempting to buy into the sell-off after prices fell sharply.

However, the earlier decline remained significant, with Ethereum price still below $1800, and XRP below $1, while Solana is still below $100 and other major tokens still facing pressure from the broader market downturn.

The rebound appears to have been driven by dip-buying after an aggressive sell-off, with easing liquidation pressure allowing prices to recover. Bitcoin’s decline below key support levels triggered forced selling among leveraged traders. As prices approached the $55,000 region, the sharp decline created an opportunity for traders to buy at lower levels, helping BTC recover rapidly.

It has been revealed that but the broader market’s underlying conditions remain fragile. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies have faced pressure from weakening technology stocks, concerns over AI valuations, higher borrowing costs and institutional withdrawals from spot Bitcoin ETFs.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $582 million in net outflows, while monthly withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion, weakening a major source of institutional demand. The combination of ETF redemptions and broader risk aversion has left the market susceptible to sharp price swings.

Bitcoin’s recovery above $60,000 is an notable short-term development, but it does not yet establish that the market has bottomed. The cryptocurrency needs to hold above reclaimed levels and regain additional resistance zones to strengthen the bullish case. A renewed breakdown could quickly erase the rebound, particularly if institutional outflows continue or broader markets remain under pressure.

The crypto market today is witnessing a sharp relief rally, but Bitcoin’s ability to sustain its recovery above $60,000 will determine whether buyers can turn the bounce into a broader reversal or whether the market faces another wave of selling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that plugShare is giving its EV charging app a big overhaul. Version 8.0 arrives worldwide for iPhone on November 10, with dark mode, a trip planner that reveals how far apart charging stops are, and a rebuilt Apple Watch app that can point you to a charger compatible with your EV.

It has been revealed that dark mode was one of the most-requested features from PlugShare users. It works across the app and follows your iPhone’s settings, so if your phone switches to dark mode at sunset, your charging map will, too.

Sources indicate that the trip planner gets a small but handy change. Each charging stop now reveals how far it is from both the start of your trip and the previous stop. So when you’re deciding whether to stretch to the next fast charger or stop sooner, the number you need is right there.

It has been revealed that plugShare now loads your saved locations, trips, and profile when you open the app or sign in, so those tabs are ready to tap. You can also open and zoom in on station photos right from their thumbnails. That’s handy when you’re trying to figure out what corner a charging station is in in a major parking lot. The app also adapts its layout to the iPhone Duo’s different screens and folded positions.

The rebuilt Watch app lists nearby charging stations with distances and directions. It uses the filters you’ve set on your iPhone, so if you’ve filtered for plugs that fit your EV, that carries over to your wrist.

Tap a station and you’ll see its PlugScore, the network that runs it, a small map, and which plugs it has, including NACS, CCS, CHAdeMO, or J1772. The list refreshes when you raise your wrist and open the app. You can also add a shortcut to a round or corner slot on your watch face.

In a recent development, the iPhone update is rolling out through the App Store. PlugShare says Android users will get dark mode and a redesign based on Google’s Material 3 in early 2027.

Humble Hauler autonomous trailer takes the truck out of trucking [update]

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less than a year after its founding, truckless trucking brand Humble Robotics has secured more than $75 million after a $51 million Series A funding round that will fuel the company’s transition from prototype to preproduction.
  • The latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners.
  • “We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself,” explains Humble Robotics founder and CEO, Eyal Cohen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than a year after its founding, truckless trucking brand Humble Robotics has secured more than $75 million after a $51 million Series A funding round that will fuel the company’s transition from prototype to preproduction.

The latest funding round for the driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform developer was led by Obvious Ventures with participation from other existing investors Eclipse and Energy Impact Partners. Humble said it will use the funding for customer pilots, testing and validation, and early manufacturing.

“We’ve spent years proving that a truck can drive itself,” explains Humble Robotics founder and CEO, Eyal Cohen. “The harder question is how to make autonomy something a freight operator can depend on every day.”.

According to recent reports, we originally covered the Humble Hauler back in May. You can check out the original article, below, then let us know what you think of the company’s prospects in the comments.

The startup that dares to ask, “Why does the Macbook driving my freight around need a whole cab?” just showed off a fully driverless, cab-less, and truck-less battery-electric freight platform designed to handle containerized cargo more efficiently than ever.

Instead of looking at the tractor and asking how to make it work without a driver, Humble looked at the trailer, itself, redesigning the container chassis as a vehicle from the ground up. The end result isn’t just an autonomous solution, it’s an overall lighter platform without a cab that saves shippers the weight of a sleeper cab, a day cab, or the truck at all.

The Humble approach is stated to improve payload efficiency of shipping containers, and intended for dock-to-dock operation.

It has been revealed that “I have dedicated my career to building electric and autonomous vehicle technology,” explains Eyal Cohen, Humble Robotics’ founder and CEO. “For the first time, freight can be fully automated all the way to the loading dock. We are making freight sustainable, safe and efficient in a way no one thought was possible. And we’re doing it with an exceptional team of industry veterans and AV experts.”.

Emerging from stealth after a $24 million funding round, Humble claims to have completed its first Humble Hauler prototype in less than six months – and they’ll soon be ready to begin autonomous testing in pilot programs with a number of logistics partners.

The vehicle uses a combination of cameras, lidar, and radar for 360-degree awareness (unhindered by seeing around a cab), and uses vision-language-action models to help the system respond to new scenarios.

According to recent reports, thanks to superior battery tech, a maturing global charging infrastructure, and a permanently damaged MidEast oil supply, there’s never been a better time to be an EV startup. Humble is hitting all the electric trailer buzzwords, too, while also touting the fact that the electric powertrain can reduce a organization’s to volatile fuel prices even as it helps produce other cost benefits like lower maintenance costs.

There is a reason why the transportation industry developed separate cabs and trailers. Trailers can be loaded or unloaded for days and are much less expensive than trucks that serve both purposes in one piece. That allows the more expensive piece of the transport puzzle to be used more and allows the trailer to be loaded and unloaded while the cab is elsewhere working or in the shop. Query whether the savings they cite will surpass the costs of not having the flexibility of a cab and trailer design.

And if a robot like this can deliver on its promises without the baked-in inefficiencies of humanoids, they might be one step closer to provide that the most efficient solution to a problem is rarely a general one, and even rarer is it a solution that looks like a human.

  • As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Tech giant on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.
  • The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, vanEck has terminated Gemini as custodian and clearing agent for three U.S. crypto ETFs. In doing so, it has made Coinbase Custody its sole remaining safekeeper, thus putting into jeopardy the Solana fund’s staking future.

As per three 8-K filings from the 19th of November, VanEck Digital Assets delivered written termination notices to Gemini Trust Tech giant on the 16th of November, with the contract set to officially end on 16th February.

The notice ended custody and clearing arrangements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL) and the VanEck Ethereum ETF (ETHV).

The third ETF, the VanEck Solana ETF (VSOL), is the most affected one in this regard, because there is no news on who will take over staking services for it. Market participants are assuming it is Coinbase, but as of now, there is no confirmation yet.

According to recent reports, as expected, the filings have opened a series of questions, as they have not established the allocation of assets between Gemini and Coinbase. This, in turn, has made it impossible to quantify precisely what Gemini is losing in dollar terms.

Industry observers note that the filing also failed to explain why VanEck chose to terminate the agreements now, with roughly three months of notice before the effective date. Moreover, they did not even address the staking question that matters most for VSOL shareholders.

This comes as the crypto ETF landscape has been in a consolidation for a while now, with Coinbase already being a custodian for most U.S. Spot crypto ETFs.

All in all, VanEck’s current decision to put an end to its Gemini arrangements has left it with a single custodian across all three funds and a massive unresolved operational gap.

What’s left now is that by 16th February, 2027, the firm will have to find a newly introduced staking provider for VSOL.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin recently climbed back to about $60,200 after briefly dipping below $56,000. The coin is now down more than half from its all-time high, and the daily chart still reveals no confirmed bottom. Most of the selling has come from spot ETF investors, many of whom have been losing money for most of the year. At the time of writing, Bitcoin Price s trading near $58,700.

ETF Buyers Hit Their Breakeven and Sold.

The average buyer of US spot Bitcoin ETFs paid about $84,000. Since February, Bitcoin has traded above that price on only eight days, all in late September and early October. The rally stopped right at that level.

Recent findings suggest that on October 21, Bitcoin closed near $84,100, almost exactly at the average ETF entry price. The next day brought the biggest ETF outflow since June. Since October 20:.

Leverage Keeps Pushing Prices Lower.

In a recent development, even after Friday’s liquidations, open futures positions are almost as high as they were on October 20. On nearly every day since then, long traders have been paying short traders to keep their bets open. Each upcoming drop forces more longs out, and that pushes prices down further.

The Fed Is Only Part of the Story.

According to recent reports, US yields hit their highest level in more than 20 years in early October, and Bitcoin has usually been lower a month after past rate hikes. But the crash only started later, and yields have eased slightly since October 20. Based on how closely Bitcoin has tracked stocks, the dollar and yields over the past year, those three would explain a fall of about 15% to 17%. Bitcoin was down 29% by Friday’s close. The rest came from selling inside crypto: ETF holders cutting losses and leveraged traders being forced out.

Industry observers note that at each of Bitcoin’s last four major lows, including the July low, the bottom came within about three weeks of peak ETF selling. Sometimes it came just before the peak and sometimes just after. Four cases are too few to call it a rule, but the idea is simple: once sellers who want out are out, the main pressure eases.

Four-week ETF selling is still close to its heaviest level since the July low, so that turn hasn’t come yet. Bitcoin has, however, moved back above the July low after briefly breaking below it.

How Low Can Bitcoin Go: Key Levels to Watch.

It has been revealed that the daily chart still has no confirmed low. The decline from the September high has no clear structure. A relief bounce is overdue, and the area to watch for it is $66,000 to $79,000. That is a zone where a bounce could stall, not a price target.

Sources indicate that crypto exchange Binance has issued a "one-letter" security warning to crypto people, urging them to carefully check website addresses before logging into their accounts. According to Binance, a fake site can be just one letter off.

A post on X by the crypto exchange pointed out that a small difference in a website URL, sometimes just one letter, can lead consumers to visit fake websites impersonating legitimate platforms.

"Sometimes the biggest red flag is just one letter," Binance wrote.

The exchange advised owners to double-check URLs before entering their login credentials. It also encouraged anyone uncertain about a website's authenticity to use Binance's official verification tool to confirm whether the URL belongs to the platform.

The Binance Verify platform allows crypto consumers to stay safe from scammers, as they can enter a URL, email address, phone number, Telegram account, or social media account to check if the source is verified and officially from Binance.

In a recent development, impersonation scams are quietly growing across the crypto space, with one of the most troubling tactics seen being the deepfake: lifelike, AI-generated impersonations of crypto executives and employees soliciting money on video calls that look and sound real enough to make anyone hesitate. The personas are fabricated, but the sophistication is genuine.

Every day, people are contacted by impersonators using the names, likenesses, and even job titles of crypto personnel, including Binance staff, to solicit investments or financial transactions via WhatsApp, Telegram, and other channels.

Binance stated that scammers prey on people's growing interest in investing and digital finance and on their trust, often masquerading as its employees or executives to exploit its credibility.

With advances in AI and deepfake technology, they can create personas that look and sound real. Crypto users are therefore urged to beware of unsolicited advice or "special opportunities" and to refrain from clicking on unknown links or URLs.

Honda highlights off its next electric motorcycle, and it’s wilder than you thought

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Honda has been getting increasingly serious about electric motorcycles, but if you want to see just how weird the company thinks the future could get, take a look at the Honda EV Outlier Concept.
  • I got a chance to see the wild-looking machine in person at EICMA in Milan, where it looked like almost nothing else on the show floor.
  • The EV Outlier Concept originally debuted at last year’s Japan Mobility Show as Honda’s attempt to imagine an electric motorcycle that isn’t simply a conventional motorcycle with the engine swapped for a battery and motor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honda has been getting increasingly serious about electric motorcycles, but if you want to see just how weird the company thinks the future could get, take a look at the Honda EV Outlier Concept.

I got a chance to see the wild-looking machine in person at EICMA in Milan, where it looked like almost nothing else on the show floor. And that’s exactly the point.

The EV Outlier Concept originally debuted at last year’s Japan Mobility Show as Honda’s attempt to imagine an electric motorcycle that isn’t simply a conventional motorcycle with the engine swapped for a battery and motor. In fact, Honda describes the concept as looking toward the future of electric motorcycles beyond 2030.

The result is certainly unconventional.

This ain’t your grandpa’s SuperCub.

Sources indicate that instead of a centrally mounted motor driving the rear wheel, the EV Outlier uses motors inside both wheels, giving it all-wheel drive and allowing Honda’s designers to completely rethink the rest of the motorcycle’s layout. The battery is housed in that large central black body, while the rider sits extremely low and behind it.

Honda describes the design philosophy with three words: “Gliding, Ecstasy, and Low.” The first refers to the smooth, nearly silent feeling of electric propulsion, while the second describes the instant acceleration and massive torque available from independently controlled front and rear motors. “Low” is more literal: Honda deliberately dropped the rider’s seating and eye position to create an entirely different sensation from a conventional motorcycle.

There’s even a bucket-style backrest designed to support the rider under hard acceleration and let the rider pivot through corners around their hips.

Cool and fun for Honda engineers to play with, but it seems a big no for reality, or at least a different road reality then mine.

Emergency tight swerves for accident avoidance? Nope, gone. Seeing even less of the road, even without a car in front of you, due to being so low? Not good for me nor the deer I don't avoid due to seeing it too late.

Unsprung mass due to hub motors - lots of literature on that topic, so I'll leave that alone.

Up front, traditional mirrors are replaced by cameras, while a wide digital cockpit can display things like lean angle, riding modes, front motor torque adjustment, and what the two wheels are doing in real time.

Industry observers note that will Honda actually build this thing? Almost certainly not exactly as you see it here. That’s what concepts are for.

But the EV Outlier is still interesting as a statement of intent. Honda is obviously still playing around with the freedom that electric drivetrains offer, and the company is asking what motorcycles could become once designers no longer have to work around engines, fuel tanks, transmissions, and traditional drivetrains.

And judging by what I saw at EICMA, Honda’s answer could get pretty wild.

Revenue ran $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier, a 13x increase. Annualize that and $1.5 trillion is roughly 34 times sales.

It has been revealed that that’s a steep raise given the macro backdrop and the Fed calling for more hikes for longer. AI stocks have been shaky over the past month and even moreso since Jensen Huang left Nvidia. Not the most confident market headed into the 2nd $1T+ IPO of the year.

So what does it mean for today’s price action? Personally, I expect a pop to the $95-$105 level that Hyperliquid has been pricing out for weeks, and it likely sees a spike higher. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the upcoming (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.

We will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diesel-electric locomotives have been barreling along America’s wide-open spaces for generations, and the century-old combination of highly efficient diesel engines spinning up generators to power high-torque electric motors has proven tough to beat. Now, Caterpillar is putting that century-old concept to work underground. Meet the CAT R3200 XE LHD.

One of the many hard-working machines moving chunks of Earth under your feet, an LHD (load, haul, and dump) machine is essentially a massive underground wheel loader designed to scoop up blasted rock, haul it through narrow mine tunnels, then dump it into trucks or ore passes. Built low and wide to fit in the tunnels, LHDs are workhorses of underground mining operations – and the new R3200 XE is CAT’s biggest yet, with a 25 ton payload and electric drive.

Before we get into the machine’s specs (the few that we have, anyway), I want to make sure understand that large-scale mining operations use obscene amounts of fuel, and a swing in site efficiency of just 1-2% can mean a huge difference in the bottom line – and fuel prices were up 27.4% (!) in August alone.

Keep the staggering weight of what that kind of fuel cost can mean to a fleet that buys fuel by the literal truckload as you read the rest of this.

Though not yet officially released by CAT, snippets of the firm’s launch video have been leaking through dealers and trade journals, and they show the massive machine powered by CAT’s newest 18.1 liter Tier 5 C18 diesel generator making 527 hp (~390 kW). That C18 reportedly sends electrons to the same electric drive system used in the company’s already successful 18-ton R2900 XE LHD.

In addition to a bigger generator and heftier payload, CAT claims the upcoming R3200 XE LHD offers reduced cycle times versus the R2900 XE with 11% better speed on grade, plus reduced maintenance and repair costs thanks to design refinements for better durability, including redesigned axle. All told, that works out to 28% more tons per hour with 8% better fuel efficiency.

That efficiency is boosted by the same baked-in ADAS tech that’s made the smaller R2900 XE a favorite, and includes the latest version of CAT AutoDig and MineStar, ensuring that the machines are easy for experienced CAT operators to set up for remote, semi-autonomous, and even fully autonomous operation using Command for Underground.

Industry observers note that we’ll post an patch once CAT makes the full rundown of official specs public, which should be sooner rather than later. When that happens, we’ll see exactly how this massive burrowing CAT stacks up against the competition from Sandvik, Epiroc, and Komatsu. In the meantime, let us know what you think of CAT’s newest electric drive machine in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Why Bitcoin Just Dropped to a 5-Month Low Near $61,300.

Three separate market pressures just collided—pushing BTC to a level not seen since July.

Bitcoin plunged 4.35% over the past 24 hours, falling to $61,300 — its lowest level since early July — as a global sell-off in AI stocks, heavy withdrawals from Bitcoin ETFs and a wave of forced liquidations sent shockwaves through crypto markets.

By Friday morning, Bitcoin was struggling to stay above $61,500, putting it on track for its seventh consecutive weekly decline.

This drop wasn’t triggered by a single event. Instead, several pressures hit the market at once: growing concerns over AI valuations, institutional investors pulling money out of Bitcoin ETFs, and leveraged traders being forced to close their positions as prices fell.

The broader pullback was driven by a retreat from riskier assets as investors questioned lofty AI valuations.

On Thursday, November 19, AI company Anthropic made its highly anticipated debut on the Nasdaq. Shares opened at $111.50 against an IPO price of $83, briefly pushing the company’s valuation above $2 trillion. However, the successful IPO failed to lift sentiment across the technology sector.

As Anthropic began trading, Bitcoin fell from around $62,700 to $62,250 within roughly 30 minutes, while broader Nasdaq losses accelerated.

By the end of the session, the Nasdaq was down 2.3%, the S&P 500 had fallen 2%, and the Dow Jones lost 2.2%.

The sell-off spread to Asia, where South Korea’s KOSPI dropped approximately 5%, triggering a temporary restriction on automated selling.

Institutional demand for Bitcoin is also showing signs of weakening, adding further pressure to an already struggling market.

According to recent reports, according to SoSoValue data, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $582.19 million in net outflows on November 19, marking the largest single-day withdrawal of the month.

It has been revealed that with the exception of a modest $8 million inflow on November 5, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have faced nearly two weeks of persistent capital withdrawals, signaling a significant pullback in institutional demand.

As spot prices broke below key support levels, leveraged derivatives traders fueled a cascade of forced selling.

Recent findings suggest that coinGlass data shows $697.35 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours. About $600M came from long positions, and $201.25M of the total was Bitcoin longs.

According to market analyst Axel Adler Jr., Bitcoin remains under significant bearish pressure, with short-term investors sitting on substantial unrealized losses. Bitcoin is currently trading 15.7% below the average cost basis of recent buyers and has remained below that level for 12 consecutive days.

Sources indicate that until BTC reclaims the short-term holder cost basis and U.S. spot ETF flows flip back into positive territory, an analyst warns that the broader market correction isn’t over yet.

In a recent development, bitcoin’s slide alongside AI stocks underscores how tightly crypto still tracks risk appetite in traditional markets. Continued ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations are likely to keep pressure on prices until broader market sentiment stabilizes.

Polestar has now fully unveiled the Formula 2030 concept, a low four-door electric sports car that previews the design of the next-generation Polestar 2 coming in 2027 and the Polestar 7 compact SUV.

The concept sits just 1,350 mm (53 inches) tall, which is lower than the Polestar 5 grand tourer, and it brings physical buttons back into the Swedish brand’s interior.

Sources indicate that we reported in September that Polestar confirmed the Formula 2030 concept after showing it privately to investors and retailers in Gothenburg. Now we get the full set of pictures and the details.

It’s the first show car built under head of design Philipp Römers, who joined from Audi in 2024.

Polestar calls the Formula 2030 a “compact practical four-door sports car” that “sits within its own segment.” It’s 4,680 mm (184.3 inches) long and 2,021 mm (79.6 inches) wide, on a 2,780 mm (109.4-inch) wheelbase.

For context, that’s about 3 inches longer than today’s Polestar 2 and roughly 5 inches lower. It’s also a bit shorter than a Tesla Model 3 and sits 3.5 inches closer to the ground. Polestar says the concept lands “somewhere between” the upcoming Polestar 2 and Polestar 7 in size.

In a recent development, the proportions are classic sports car: long hood, short overhangs, the cabin pushed back over significant rear haunches, and 22-inch center-lock wheels. There are gold Brembo calipers behind those wheels and Öhlins dampers on display in the trunk.

Up front, Polestar kept its “Dual Blade” headlights, now set into an aero wing over a shark nose and a deep splitter. The automaker says this is the face of the next-generation Polestar 2 planned for 2027.

There’s a single vertical windshield wiper, like on a race car, and a LiDAR unit that hides under an aerodynamic shroud and only shows itself when the car is driving autonomously.

It has been revealed that the rear is where things change the most. Polestar dropped the full-width light bar, which is on just about every EV these days, for what it calls “Single Blade” rear lights. It claims they are being introduced here “ahead of series production.”.

Römers described the concept as a “bold evolution” of the brand’s existing design:.

“It is a physical embodiment of how we apply Polestar’s core values of design, performance and sustainability to the next production cars.”.

The rear doors are hinged at the back and there’s no B-pillar, so the whole side opens up to four individual seats.

The interior is built around the driver. A curved 20-inch display, which Polestar calls the “HyperDIM,” is mounted directly on the steering column, and a 12.2-inch center screen sits in the center tunnel.

According to recent reports, but the bigger news is below that screen. Polestar added a panel of eight physical controls for the most-used functions, and owners could swap between types of controls, like rocker switches or rotary knobs, and program what each one does.

Polestar notes it is “committing to rebalance the mix of physical and digital.” Juan Pablo Bernal, the firm’s head of interior design, put it plainly:.

“As a performance brand, we see a renewed focus on the driver, and so we re-balance the digital and physical. We introduce physical buttons and controls.”.

That’s a major change for a brand whose recent cars run almost everything through the center touchscreen.

The cabin also physically changes with the drive mode. There are three of them: Performance, Normal, and Autonomous. In Performance, the center screen drops flush into the console and the steering wheel and its display pull closer to the driver. In Autonomous, the wheel and the seat move away from each other.

The four seats use inflatable bolsters that shape themselves to each occupant, and the seat backs are made of a flax-based composite instead of virgin plastic. Google Gemini is built in, like in Polestar’s production cars.

Sources indicate that the cargo area is the strangest part of the car. The rear opens as a clamshell, and the trunk floor is transparent, with custom Polestar bags strapped down underneath it with gold straps.

Up front, the frunk holds two race helmets and a fire extinguisher, framed by a gold strut brace.

Recent findings suggest that now for what’s missing. Polestar didn’t release a single powertrain spec. No battery size, no range, no power output, and no price. This is a design study, and Polestar isn’t saying it will build it.

What it does say is that “various design attributes” from the concept will show up on the next Polestar 2 in 2027 and the Polestar 7 in 2028. Those are two of the four new models Polestar looks to launch in three years, and the 7 is going to be built in Europe.

Europe is where this matters, since Polestar is shut out of the US under the federal connected-vehicle rule. The concept made its debut during the media drive of the Polestar 4 SUV.

Polestar always impresses me with its design, and this is no exception with this new head of design.

Industry observers note that the proportions are sharp. Long hood, cabin pushed back, big haunches, and a roofline lower than the Polestar 5’s on a car with four doors and four real seats. If the next Polestar 2 keeps even half of this stance, it’s going to be the best-looking car in its segment.

Sources indicate that I have loved Polestar from the day they debuted. Every car they design is a work of art and I love their commitment to transparency and sustainablitity. The 2023 Polestar 2 is still one of my favorite cars I've ever owned. I've driven the 3 and the 4 and both were fantastic. The fit and finish, ride and build quality, and NVH were all excellent. The upgraded 3 was probably going to be my next car in 2027 until they were forced to withdraw from the US. I think their future with the new 2 and 7 are bright and I'm still hoping (though I'm not holding my breath) that they will return to the US at some point. If the 5 was available here, I'd buy it today.

Recent findings suggest that I don’t know about the trunk of this thing. Polestar itself calls the rear “UFO-esque,” and between the wraparound glass, the clamshell and the see-through floor, it’s a lot. But everything else on this car is pretty sharp.

Industry observers note that polestar is putting physical controls back in its cars and saying so in plain words. The way they talk about it makes it sound like you can expect that of upcoming production vehicles.

According to recent reports, now the usual caveat. A concept car doesn’t fix a balance sheet. Polestar lost $842 million in the first half of this year on a negative gross margin. Design has never been Polestar’s problem. Building these cars and selling them at a profit is.

Cardano fell to $0.133, a five-month low on Saturday as the crypto market sell-off deepened. At the time of writing, Cardano had slightly rebounded, up 1.82% in the last 24 hours to $0.144, as a substantial buy wall of 3.96 million ADA emerged on Binance, offering a layer of support as sellers pressured the cryptocurrency.

A buy wall occurs when a large volume of buy orders is concentrated around a particular price level on an exchange's order book. Such an order cluster can indicate that traders are prepared to purchase an asset at that price, potentially slowing further declines if selling pressure meets sufficient demand.

In a recent development, in Cardano's case, the 3.96 million ADA order cluster that occurred below the $0.14 level revealed a notable level of buying interest. As the orders at this level were filled, they helped absorb selling pressure for Cardano and provided short-term support for the price.

Current data from CoinGlass shows that open interest is down 1.98%, mostly due to shorts closing, although funding remains negative at −0.0099%, with shorts paying longs.

The next key levels to watch for ADA, according to on-chain data provided by CoinGlass, are $0.1462, which has a short liquidation cluster, and $0.1375, which has a long liquidation cluster.

Dijkstra hard fork preparations continue to progress, with Intersect, a Cardano-based entity, revealing what might come next in the coming weeks.

in about one or two weeks, the Cardano Node 11.2.3 release (GitHub), the Node RC 2026w47 release for the Musashi network (GitHub), and the publication of v6 of CAP-12 to the Constitutional Amendment Portal are anticipated.

In about two to three weeks, the Cardano Node 11.3 pre-release is anticipated, while an upgrade to the Constitution governance action on-chain is expected in about one month.

Dijkstra requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. These include Constitutional guardrails (Update Constitution) and Plutus V4 (Parameter Update).

CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" proposes to amend the Constitution to accommodate new block type definitions and set guardrails for new updatable parameter types introduced with Protocol Version 12.

Industry observers note that according to Davis, Cardano accounts for just around 1% of Solana’s daily consumers, highlighting the stark difference in activity between the two networks. The gap reportedly extends beyond user numbers, with Cardano recording only about 0.3% of Solana’s perpetual futures trading volume.

According to recent reports, the revenue figures paint an even more challenging picture for the Cardano ecosystem. Davis estimates that Cardano generates roughly 0.2% of the application revenue recorded across Solana’s ecosystem, further highlighting the difference in economic activity between the competing networks.

Based on these figures, Davis delivered a particularly harsh assessment of Cardano, describing it as a “largely failed blockchain.” His criticism centers on the contrast between Cardano’s nine-year journey and Solana’s ability to build a considerably larger user base and generate more trading activity and application revenue in a shorter period.

Recent findings suggest that the latest criticism follows a series of similar remarks from Davis about Cardano’s adoption challenges. As ZyCrypto previously reported, the analyst had also taken aim at Cardano over its relatively small user base, questioning the network’s ability to attract and retain consumers despite years of development.

Despite his harsh assessment of Cardano’s fundamentals, Davis has occasionally expressed optimism about ADA’s price prospects.

In November 2025, for instance, he suggested that Cardano could stage a rally similar to XRP’s 2024 surge, pointing to the strength of its community and brand as potential catalysts.

More recently, on September 28, Davis argued that Cardano’s “cult following” could help drive ADA back toward $1, with further upside potentially taking the token to $1.50 or even $2.

However, these bullish price projections focused more on speculative market demand and Cardano’s dedicated community than on measurable improvements in network adoption or ecosystem activity.

According to Santiment’s data, Lido Staked Ethereum (stETH) recorded net outflows of 4,186 tokens from exchanges, marking its largest single-day outflow since the 30th of May.

As a result, there has been a decline in the amount of stETH immediately available on exchanges for potential selling.

This comes as Ethereum was trading near $1,753.91 at press time, after a drop of 2.9% in the past 24 hours.

At the same time, around 836,798 ETH is presently waiting to enter Ethereum’s validator network. Of this, the estimated waiting period currently stands at 14 days and 13 hours, with a processing rate (churn) of 256 ETH per epoch.

Meanwhile, the exit queue presents a different picture wherein around 164,005 ETH is waiting to leave the validator network, with an estimated waiting period of 3 days and 20 hours.

Looking at the broader picture, Ethereum right now has approximately 773,650 active validators, with 44.6 million ETH staked. This represents around 36.5% of Ethereum’s total supply, while the network’s annual percentage rate (APR) stands at 2.42%.

So now, if exchange outflows continue, the entry queue remains elevated, and ETH prices begin stabilizing, these developments could strengthen the argument that investors are positioning themselves for the longer term rather than preparing to sell into market weakness.

Interestingly, all of this coincided with a recent report by AMBCrypto where Ethereum’s staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high of 36.3%, with approximately 44.5 million ETH locked in staking, up from 42.1 million in mid-August.

Meanwhile, institutional players such as BitMine and SharpLink continue expanding their staking activities, with BitMine holding 5.22 million staked ETH and earning $121.4 million from staking and validation.

Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
  • Sources indicate that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) stated in a report published on Thursday.
  • "Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.

Sources indicate that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) stated in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais said in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that the 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.

Industry observers note that IOSCO said the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day.".

In a recent development, swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report remarked. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.

Because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO said. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.

Wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has said. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.

The report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.

Recent findings suggest that layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report said.

Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has mentioned the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.

Sources indicate that IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to enhancement cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.

Most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.

No surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO stated it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.

Industry observers note that quantum hardware is advancing quickly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has remarked it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lucid (LCID) claims service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.
  • Sources indicate that the automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans.
  • In a recent development, lucid declared the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lucid (LCID) claims service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.

Sources indicate that the automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.

In a recent development, lucid declared the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings. Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.

The hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.

Sources indicate that that’s a significant hiring push for a organization that laid off 18% of its workforce in June, its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.

According to recent reports, and owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.

Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, stated the firm is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”.

Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:.

Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.

Outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first company-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.

Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.

A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-glitch. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.

Sources indicate that it’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.

For context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.

This is the right move, and it’s overdue.

Lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if we found its software wasn’t ready. But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.

So growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a big deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.

Recent findings suggest that the problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.
